refactor(ci): read review-lane status jobs from merge-holds REVIEW_LANES (#19111)

No related issue: deepening candidate c7, owner-approved (architecture
docs/owner-decisions.md row 433)

## Summary

Candidate c7 ("one review-lane reader") asked for one owner for every
reader of the review lanes' state. Mapping the readers found two real
copies of a table that `merge-holds.mjs` `REVIEW_LANES` already owns.
This PR removes both copies. The lane-run selection pair the scan named
(ci-status `lane_run` and `rerun-ci-status.sh` `newest`) is left as it
is, for the reasons under Verification.

## Fix

- `clear-escalations.mjs` `LANE_RECORDS`: the six status job names per
lane now come from `REVIEW_LANES`, which the module already imported.
The names and their order are the same as before.
- ci-status `Clear a cost-only review hold the owner decided`: the step
now prints the lane list from the base commit's `REVIEW_LANES` through
node, in place of an inline two-line copy. The step already runs the
base's `refsIssue`, `mergedParents`, `baseMergeCarry` and `unranHead`
the same way. Its "changes a review-lane workflow" test is now the
base's `laneChange`, with the same 300-file cap and the same two paths.
`unranHead` requires `ran` in `REVIEW_LANES` order, and the loop now
follows that order by construction.
- No new export: `REVIEW_LANES` and `laneChange` are already on main, so
the base-loaded module needs no stacked PR.
- A `bump: none` pr-pipeline changeset.

Behavior: every pass and every keep is unchanged. Two keep messages are
different:
- With an unreadable base `merge-holds.mjs`, the step now keeps the hold
at "the review lanes could not be read". Before, it kept it at a later
`holds_js` call.
- A compare with no file list now keeps the hold at "changes no file
list". Before, the message was "do not parse".

## Verification

Reader map, before:

| Reader | Reads | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-require-checks.yml` `Require both review lanes on this head`,
`lane_run` (~:7530) | the head's pull_request runs listing, else the
per-workflow listing | newest run by id for path, sha, event and head
repository, optionally filtered to the PR; the listing counts only when
whole |
| `rerun-ci-status.sh` `newest`/`file_runs` (:86-107) | the same listing
| the same selector, with no PR filter; a failed listing read falls back
to the per-workflow listing, where ci-status fails closed |
| `pr-require-checks.yml` cost-hold step (~:5752) | per-lane runs by
branch, status jobs, `claude-lane-hold` notices | **inline copy of
REVIEW_LANES job names** and an inline review-lane path test |
| `clear-escalations.mjs` `LANE_RECORDS` / `reviewLanesClean` | the
per-workflow listing (strictly fewer than 100 runs), jobs, records |
**copy of REVIEW_LANES job names** |
| `merge-holds.mjs` `REVIEW_LANES`, `laneChange` | owner | checked
against `.github/lane-registry.json` by `lane-registry.test.mjs` |
| `resolve-pr.mjs` | reads no review-lane state: "lane" there means the
pr-merge lane and the lanes App | none |

After: the cost-hold step and `LANE_RECORDS` read `REVIEW_LANES` and
`laneChange`, so the two copies are gone.

The lane-run selector pair is not merged. Sharing it would need:
- a new file that both workflows load: ci-status from the base-config
checkout, `rerun-ci-status` from main's tip;
- two stacked PRs;
- a new dependency of the review-lanes step's main path on the
base-config checkout, which can turn ci-status red on a checkout flake
and add merge latency.

All of that to save a 4-line jq filter, and the two callers keep
different read-failure policies anyway. The step's inline `lanes` list
(~:7245) also stays as it is. It is in a different order from
`REVIEW_LANES`, and that order decides which job name the error messages
show.

No API calls change: the cost-hold step adds two local node runs on
files it already reads.

feat(intake-triage): run /work-items:triage --ci on the read runner's verdict mode (#19060)

Closes #18859


## Summary

The intake lane's model job moves off the ci-workflows intake reusable
onto this repository's read runner, as decided (option A2, refined; Q69
and Q70). `triage-issue` runs `/work-items:triage --issue <n> --ci` in
`pr-run-activity-read.yml`'s new verdict mode with the read skill tools
only (Read, Glob, Grep, Skill). The verdict is structured output, held
to one schema that ships with the skill. A no-model `post-triage` job
checks it and posts the comment, labels and Issue Type on the job's
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, so the comment's author stays `github-actions[bot]`.
`apply-verdict.mjs` and `admit.mjs` are unchanged.

## Fix

- **Schema, defined once.**
`plugins/work-items/skills/triage/schemas/ci-verdict.schema.json`, with
an optional `type`. `check-ci-verdict.mjs` reads it (and takes
`--schema` for a narrowed copy). `collect-base-activity` copies it for
the launcher with `size`, `complexity` and `uncertainty` narrowed to
enums from `models.issue-dimensions.fields`. `write-intake-issue.mjs`
narrows `type` to the enabled Issue Types, or drops it.
- **`ci-mode.md`.** Steps 3 and on are rewritten: the model runs neither
script and returns the verdict as structured output. It reads
`open_issues` and `merged_pulls` from `issue.json`, and the repository's
`## Triage rules` in `docs/conventions/work-items.md`.
- **Read runner verdict mode (`issue-verdict`).** It admits a dispatch
naming the issue, claims no lease, skips the stale-file and prior-work
checks, writes `issue.json` (newest 200 open issues, latest 100 merged
PRs), and carries the structured output through the existing scan slot.
The verdict is uploaded as `triage-verdict-<issue>-<attempt>`, and the
scan job exports its SHA-256. The scan refuses a verdict run that
carries a patch, replies or an outcome.
- **Trigger gate: exactly today's sources.** `check-trusted-trigger`
gains `bot-sender-ids` and `issue-author`. Verdict mode passes
`41898282` and the lanes App: an issues event proceeds only as `opened`
by its own author, and an issue or a dispatch only from a listed human
or one of those two bots. A re-run needs a listed human.
- **`intake-triage.yml`.** It runs three credential legs with handoff
jobs, as `work-resolve-issue.yml` does, then `post-triage`
(`.github/scripts/intake-triage/post-triage.mjs`, a port of the
reusable's apply job). `post-triage` checks the verdict's SHA-256,
`check-ci-verdict.mjs` and `set-dimensions.sh --dry-run` before any
write. A missing or refused verdict applies nothing and fails the job,
so the triage sweep runs the issue again. The repository's own rubric
rules (the `Cost decided:` line, re-entry (d), the blocked-by-issue stop
rule and done-when items a lane run cannot do) move to
`docs/conventions/work-items.md`.
- **Config.** `pr-pipeline.yaml` gets the `triage-issue` and
`post-triage` activities and slots, `triage-verdict` joins the
`applied-by` schema enum, and `resolve-config` outputs
`applied-by-triage-verdict`. `lane-grants.json`, `lane-funding.json` and
`check-read-caller-keys.mjs` gain the intake rows.

## Verification

- `node --test` over the changed suites: `callers.test.mjs` (309),
`check-trusted-trigger.test.mjs` (520),
`collect-base-activity.test.mjs`, `post-triage.test.mjs`,
`write-intake-issue.test.mjs`, `check-ci-verdict.test.mjs`,
`apply-verdict.test.mjs`, `triage-sweep.test.mjs`,
`label-unblocked.test.mjs`, `resolve.test.mjs`, `lane-grants.test.mjs`
and the other suites that read these workflows. All pass.
- Shell suites `check-read-caller-keys.test.sh`,
`read-lane-broker-check.test.sh`, `read-runner-dispatcher-gate.test.sh`,
`write-runner-never-rules.test.sh`, `pr-unblock-trusted-base.test.sh`
and `act-turns-denied.test.sh` all pass.
`scripts/check-read-caller-keys.sh` is clean, `actionlint` is clean, and
`scripts/check-affected.sh --uncommitted` passes 22 checks.
- Not run: any eval, and no live intake run.

## Loosened checks

- `.github/actions/resolve-config/callers.test.mjs`, "every caller of a
reusable holding model legs passes the transcript key": the minimum
caller count drops from `>= 3` to `>= 2`. The intake caller moved from
the ci-workflows intake reusable to `pr-run-activity-read.yml`, so one
fewer caller holds model legs through a ci-workflows reusable; the two
left are `pr-review-hosted.yml` and `pr-review-security-hosted.yml`, and
each must still pass the transcript key. The read runner's transcripts
are checked by the lane-transcript puller tests, which now list
`triage-issue`.
- `.github/scripts/intake-triage/apply-verdict.test.mjs`, "offers
exactly the flags and typed fields the verdict reads": each dimension
option key now only has to match the schema's `pattern`, where before it
had to equal the schema's enum, and `required` now only has to include
the five verdict fields, where before it had to equal them. The skill's
schema no longer carries the repository's dimension enums: the read
runner writes them into a per-run copy, and
`.github/actions/collect-base-activity/collect-base-activity.test.mjs`
asserts the exact enums the runner writes. `check-ci-verdict.mjs` and
`post-triage.mjs` check every verdict against that per-run schema before
any write.

## Related

- Not in this PR: `.github/scripts/intake-triage/triage-rubric.txt` is
no longer passed to a model, but it stays in place because
`refine.test.mjs`, `reentry-prompt.test.mjs`, `apply-verdict.test.mjs`,
the `reentry-eval` harness and `merge-holds.mjs` still read it. Retiring
it is a follow-up.
- UNVERIFIED: whether the lanes token broker's `/check` allows the new
`intake-triage / triage-issue` read activity on `issues` and
`workflow_dispatch`. `pr-run-activity.md` says `issues` from
`intake-triage.yml` and `workflow_dispatch` on `main` are allowed, but
the azure-iac code was not read.

perf(babysit-prs): let the verdict reader hand over the pass it judged (#19085)

No related issue: deepening candidate c5, owner-approved (architecture
docs/owner-decisions.md row 433)

## Summary

First of two stacked PRs that remove ci-status's second read of the
pr-verify pass in the merge
queue. `babysit_verify_evidence.py evidence` gains `--pass-out <file>`:
on an allow at the head it
writes the objects the judgment already read (each counted pass at the
head with its run, the
first pass's verdict.json, the closing issues). The printed report does
not change, so pr-merge's
enable-auto-merge caller (`enable-auto-merge.mjs`) sees no difference.

The workflow change that uses the flag is the second PR. They are split
because ci-status runs this
script from main's checkout (`VERIFY_EVIDENCE_SCRIPT: .base/...`,
`pr-require-checks.yml:6616`; `.base`
is checked out at main's tip, `pr-require-checks.yml:5254-5259`). A
workflow that passed the new flag
in the same change would run against main's old script in its own merge
group and fail closed. This
PR must merge first.

## Fix

- `Reader._run_state` keeps the `_run_fields` of each run it reads live
(`_pass_runs`).
`_closing_issues` keeps the closing issues trimmed to `totalCount`,
`number` and `nameWithOwner`
(`_closing_refs`), the shape the workflow's GraphQL read returns.
`_evidence` keeps the counted
  passes at the head (`_head_passes`).
- `Reader.pass_link(number, head)` returns `{head, verdicts, record,
closing}`. `verdicts` holds each
counted pass as `{name, verdict, runId, artifact, run}`, the shape
merge-holds.mjs `verdictHold`
reads. `record` is the verdict.json of the first pass in name order
(pass before pass-notes,
undigested first, then as listed). That is the pass the workflow's bash
judged with `linkHold`. It
is not always `_newest(passes)`, so a record the judgment did not
download is downloaded once (the
download the step makes today). A record that does not read is `null`,
which `linkHold` holds.
- `--pass-out` writes `pass_link` for an allow at the head. Any refusal
writes no pass, no record and
no closing issues, which matches what the step's bash gives
merge-holds.mjs today in FAIL index
  mode on a refusal (`listed=false`, `pr-require-checks.yml:7016-7020`).
- A source-control changelog fragment (patch).

## Verification

- `test_babysit_verify_index.py` `PassOut` (4 new tests): an allow
writes the expected file and makes
exactly one zip, one `actions/runs/1` and one closing-issues read in the
whole judgment. A FAIL
writes no pass. With two passes where `_newest` picks pass-notes, the
record is `pass`'s (bash's
pick) after one extra download. A record that does not download is
`null`.
- babysit-prs package suite: `uvx --with pytest-xdist pytest -n 4
plugins/source-control/skills/babysit-prs/scripts/tests`:
  4715 passed, 20 skipped.
- `selection-audit.sh trace --strict` on `test_babysit_verify_index.py`:
no gap.
- Call savings are measured on the second PR, which removes the reads.

## Related

- Measurement and design: `.work/gh-optimization/c5-1125/finding.md`
(local).
-
[#19087](https://github.com/melodic-software/claude-code-plugins/pull/19087):
the workflow change
  that uses this flag. It is stacked on this PR and merges after it.

perf(pr-pipeline): serve repeated GitHub GETs as conditional reads in the shared client (#19084)

No related issue: deepening candidate c2, owner-approved (architecture
docs/owner-decisions.md row 433)

## Summary

The shared GitHub client now has one conditional-read store. When a job
repeats a GET of the same URL with the same token, the request carries
`If-None-Match` with the kept ETag, and a 304 returns the kept body.
GitHub: "Making a conditional request does not count against your
primary rate limit if a `304` response is returned and the request was
made while correctly authorized with an Authorization header" ([REST
best practices, Use conditional requests if
appropriate](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/using-the-rest-api/best-practices-for-using-the-rest-api#use-conditional-requests-if-appropriate),
read 2026-11-25). The gate's inputs are still answered by GitHub. A 304
means GitHub confirmed the kept body is current, so no verdict changes.

## Fix

- `github-client.mjs`: adds `readStore(dir)` and `conditionalReads(send,
store)`. `createGitHub` wraps its retrying sender with them.
- Only GETs are conditional. The key is the full URL plus the
Authorization header.
- The store is in memory for each client. When `GITHUB_READ_STORE` names
a directory, entries are also written there (one file per key, mode
0600), so a later step of the same job can use them. Nothing outlives
the job: no cache, no artifact.
- It fails closed. Any answer other than a 304 to a request the store
made conditional is returned exactly as before. A 304 with no kept
answer still throws `GitHubError` 304. A body `retryServerErrors` would
resend is never kept. A store file that cannot be read, or that names
another URL, counts as absent. A GET that carries its own
`If-None-Match` passes through untouched, so `resolve-pr.mjs`'s
empty-listing ETag reuse is unchanged.
- A replay keeps the kept headers but takes the 304's `x-ratelimit-*`
values, so `onResponse` throttlers see current readings.
- Reuses or replaces the existing conditional-read code rather than
adding a second copy:
- `budgetedFetch` (`request-budget.mjs`) drops its own ETag map and
calls `conditionalReads`.
- The trigger gate's `pagesSeen` memo (re-run record listing) is
removed. The client's store now does that job, and the existing tests
for it already go through a real `createGitHub` and pass unchanged.
- `check-trusted-trigger.mjs` `resolveRunPull` now reads
`commits/{sha}/pulls?per_page=100&page=1`, the first-page URL
`resolve-pr.mjs` `pullsOfCommit` reads.
- `pr-verify.yml` sets `GITHUB_READ_STORE: ${{ runner.temp
}}/github-reads` only on the resolver and gate steps of the key job. The
subscription and fallback jobs are re-rendered by
`scripts/sync-credential-legs.mjs`.
- Out of scope: the bash conditional readers (`pr-require-checks.yml`
review-wait poll, `rerun-ci-status.sh`, `handoff-evidence.sh`) run in
another language and stay as they are.

## Verification

Measured before the change (method:
`.work/gh-monitor/limits/gh-job-calls.jsonl`, the job-end `api-routes`
notices). I counted each job's route counts once per run attempt, over
the 7 full days 2026-11-18 to 2026-11-24 (UTC). The `routes` counts
already leave out 304s, so every repeat counted here is a charged call.
Script: `.work/c2/measure.py`.

| repeat served conditionally | where | per day, measured | saved per
day |
|---|---|---|---|
| A: `commits/{sha}/pulls`, resolver step then gate step, same SHA, same
`github.token` | `resolve-pr.mjs:555`, `check-trusted-trigger.mjs:170`
(base) | 313 (2,193 in 7 days; 308 in the 24 h to 2026-11-25 14:00Z) |
~313: the two reads are seconds apart |
| B: dispatcher run read twice in one gate process |
`check-trusted-trigger.mjs:354`, then `:300` (`requireRecorded`) | 300
`/ Run` jobs on the dispatcher path (2,102 in 7 days) | up to 300; the
share answered 304 is not measured, because the dispatcher run may still
be changing |

Expected after: about 313 to 613 fewer charged core calls a day. At the
same 2026-11-25 14:00Z cut, Check Intent Subscription's
`commits/{sha}/pulls` drops from 2 to 1 charged read per full-judgment
run, and the second shows up as `not-modified=` in the job's `api-calls`
notice. The 600-700 a day the deepening scan estimated is the upper end.
The measured floor is 313.

Live check (3 calls): a conditional re-read of
`commits/d2eed45.../pulls?per_page=100&page=1` 5 s after the first read
answered `HTTP/2.0 304 Not Modified`. The same path without the query
answered the same ETag. Even so, the store keys by exact URL, which is
why the gate's URL was aligned.

Merge latency: no added waits. A conditional read is the same request
with one more header.

Tests:
- New `createGitHub` tests in `check-trusted-trigger.test.mjs` cover:
  - a 304 replays the kept body with the 304's rate-limit headers
  - a changed answer is returned and kept
- fail-closed paths: a 304 with no kept answer, and a 404, 403 or 500 to
a conditional GET
  - an unparsable body is never kept
  - a caller's own `If-None-Match` passes through
  - a POST is never conditional
- the directory store carries entries to a later client on the same
token only
  - an unreadable or wrong-URL store file counts as absent
- Every `.test.mjs` that imports a changed module, tests a module that
imports one, or reads `pr-verify.yml`: 81 suites, 7,250 pass, 0 fail.
- `lane-lib` package `node --test`: 309 pass. `pr-unblock` package:
1,572 pass. `scripts/ci-lanes-pr-hold.test.sh`: 356 pass.
- `scripts/sync-credential-legs.mjs --check` is clean.
- `selection-audit.sh trace --strict` on the two changed suites reports
2 gaps. Both predate this change: `workflow.test.mjs` reads two
standards schema fixtures its `test-scope` line omits, and #19080 adds
exactly those two files to that line.

## Related

- #19080 (c1) edits `resolve-pr.mjs`, `pr-verify.yml` and
`workflow.test.mjs`. This branch does not touch `resolve-pr.mjs`. Its
`pr-verify.yml` and `workflow.test.mjs` lines sit outside #19080's
hunks, so the two should merge in either order.
- `pr-verify.yml` has no `workflow_call` trigger.
`check-trusted-trigger`'s inputs and outputs are unchanged.

fix(ci): read the eval select path list the same with CRLF line endings (#19120)

No related issue: found while dispatching eval compare runs for
https://github.com/melodic-software/claude-code-plugins/pull/19114 and
https://github.com/melodic-software/claude-code-plugins/pull/19115 on
Windows.

## Summary

`select-plugins.mjs` read its stdin path list split on `\n` only. A list
with CRLF line endings (what `select-cases.py` sends on Windows, where
`text=True` writes `\r\n`) left a trailing `\r` on every path, so
`PLUGIN_PATH` matched none of them and every refusal was skipped: the
script exited 0 and `/evals:plugin-eval select` reported that compare
mode would accept a pull request CI then refused. The check fails open
on input it did not parse.

## Fix

- `.github/scripts/plugin-eval/select-plugins.mjs`: split stdin on
`/\r?\n/`, so a CRLF list is read exactly like an LF one.
- `.github/scripts/plugin-eval/select-plugins.test.mjs`: one test feeds
a refused path beside an eval file with LF and with CRLF line endings
and asserts the refusal line itself both times (exit code alone is not
enough: the unreadable-tree refusal already exits 1 without `--repo`).

## Verification

- Before the fix the CRLF arm failed (`AssertionError`, no `h.sh`
refusal line); after it, `node --test --test-concurrency=4
.github/scripts/plugin-eval/select-plugins.test.mjs` passes 37 of 37.
- CI runs on Linux and was never affected; this fixes local `select` on
Windows.

## Related

- None.
